name: 1st Gen Society
description: 1stGen Society is committed to providing a brave and welcoming environment to all first generation, low-income (FGLI) students and allies. The mission and purpose of the club will be to serve, provide and enhance the personal and academic experience of FGLI students on campus. From all backgrounds, we aim to connect members as a community united by the vision of equality and pride in our diverse identities.

name: 2027 Class Council
description: The Class of 2027 Class Council is an organization dedicated to promoting the Class of 2027. The Council plans and runs activities targeted toward the class, promotes class unity and spirit, and, above all, strives to be a positive influence within the class and the greater University community.

name: Active Minds
description: Active Minds is a national organization focused on raising mental health awareness, fighting mental health stigma, and inspiring positive change on college campuses. Our chapter works with UHS, UCC, and various student organizations and organizes campus-wide events aiming at educating the student body on issues of mental health, challenging stigmatizing beliefs, and providing a safe and positive environment for students to share their experiences. We also have a voice in conversations with college administration regarding the campus climate surrounding mental health and mental healthcare.

name: Actuarial Science Club
description: to empower students with the knowledge, skills, and professional connections necessary to succeed in the actuarial field, while fostering a collaborative community that promotes academic excellence, career development, and industry awareness.

name: After Hours
description: After Hours is the University of Rochester's premier all-gender a cappella group. We are a group of talented, creative, and passionate musicians from all backgrounds who come together to make vibrant and memorable music. Each semester, we prepare a set of self-arranged and self-choreographed songs for our showcase. We also perform in collaboration with other student organizations on campus and at events within the Rochester community.

name: Agape Christian Fellowship
description: We are a multi-campus, multi-ethnic Christian fellowship with large group meetings every Friday night, weekly prayer meetings, small group Bible studies throughout the week, and community service opportunities throughout the year. Rides are always provided for Sunday service at The Well where we join with the local Rochester community as the body of Christ.

name: Alexander Hamilton Society
description: The Alexander Hamilton Society is a nonpartisan organization that aims to promote education, career resources, and vigorous debate and intellectual discourse for University of Rochester Students interested in pursuing careers in foreign policy, national security, and global affairs.

name: Alliance for Diversity in Science and Engineering
description: The mission of the ADSE chapter at the University of Rochester is to increase the representation and visibility of underrepresented groups (women, African Americans, Latinos/as, Native Americans, members of the LGBTQA community, people with disabilities, and DREAMers) in the STEM fields. The UR ADSE chapter will serve as a platform for the scholarship and professional development of minority students in the pursuit of advanced degrees and careers in STEM. Our goals are to connect scientists across our campus, showcase non-traditional career paths and minority experiences in academia, industry

name: Alpha Delta Phi
description: The mission of the Alpha Delta Phi Fraternity is to provide a comprehensive and positive personal growth experience for all undergraduate and alumni brothers: social, ethical, leadership, scholastic, community service, and literary.

name: Alpha Epsilon Pi
description: Alpha Epsilon Pi was founded to provide opportunities for the Jewish college man seeking the best possible college and fraternity experience. We have maintained the integrity of our purpose by strengthening our ties to the Jewish community and serving as a link between high school and career.

name: Alpha Kappa Psi
description: At Alpha Kappa Psi, we believe in pursuing our passions and supporting each other in everything we do. We know that by working together we can excel professionally, build more meaningful relationships, and have fun at the same time. Our chapter consists of business leaders, engineers, musicians, athletes, future doctors, and more. We are truly diverse but united by our drive to work hard and reach higher. name: Alpha Phi
description: Alpha Phi International Fraternity is a membership organization dedicated to promoting sisterhood, cultivating leadership, encouraging intellectual curiosity and advocating service. Alpha Phi develops character for a lifetime.

name: Alpha Phi Omega, Mu Lambda Chapter
description: Through its mission of preparing campus and community leaders through service, Alpha Phi Omega is committed to bringing together college students in a national service fraternity in the fellowship of principles derived from the Scout Oath and of the Law of the Boy Scouts of America; to develop Leadership, to promote Friendship, and to provide Service to humanity; and further the freedom that is our national, educational and intellectual heritage. Founded on the Cardinal Principles of Leadership, Friendship and Service. It provides its members the opportunity to develop leadership skills as the

name: Alpine Skiing
description: Our mission is to provide both an educational and a recreational atmosphere for competitive alpine ski racing at the University.

name: Alzheimer’s Awareness Association
description: The Alzheimer's Association is a national organization dedicated to fighting Alzheimer’s disease. It is currently the leading voluntary health organization in Alzheimer's care, support, and research. They work on national and local levels to accelerate global research, spread awareness, fundraise, and fight for care initiatives. At the University of Rochester, our mission is to honor and represent the Alzheimer's Association by advocating for Alzheimer's Disease. We aim to achieve this by fundraising, volunteering, and raising awareness within our campus community.

name: American Institute of Chemical Engineers
description: The objectives of this chapter shall be to promote the professional development of its members through its programs, and to contribute to the development of chemical engineering at the University of Rochester through activities involving faculty and student members.

name: American Sign Language Club
description: Our goal as a club is to spread awareness of the Deaf and ASL communities, as well as providing a space where those learning ASL can come together and practice the language in an immersive environment while learning Deaf culture and etiquette.

name: American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology
description: The mission of the ASBMB student chapter at the University of Rochester is to increase accessibility to research, science, and career education on campus and in the greater Rochester area, with a focus on underrepresented populations.

name: American Society of Mechanical Engineers
description: To be the premier organization for promoting the art, science and practice of mechanical and multidisciplinary engineering and allied sciences to our diverse communities throughout the world.

name: Anime Interest Floor
description: Mission The Anime Interest Floor (AIF) aims to promote and develop an interest in and enjoyment of anime and manga at the University of Rochester. We are a community that shares personal experiences and reflects on Anime and manga that we watch/read for fun. We create a fun environment that is all inclusive. AIF is on the 7th floor of Anderson and is home to a manga library with over 1000+ titles, a casual showing room, and a fun arts and crafts closet. name: Asian American Alliance
description: The Asian American Alliance at the University of Rochester is committed to empowering Asian Pacific Islander Desi Americans (APIDA) through political activism, community engagement, and social awareness. We strive for collaborative relationships with the Rochester community, activist groups, and other POC (person of color) groups. AAA will provide a platform for the organization and expression of views and interests of APIDA students at the University of Rochester. Our goal is to tackle APIDA issues from social and political perspectives while still encompassing the intricacies of diverse Asia

name: Association for the Development of Interest in the Indian Subcontinent
description: The University of Rochester's ADITI exists to provide an opportunity to interact and share the history, culture, and experiences of the Indian subcontinent. The purpose of our association is to promote and express the cultural and ethnic diversity of South Asia, which includes the following countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Over the course of the year, we showcase the heritage of our cultures through music, dance, and cinematic diversity of the Indian subcontinent culture. We are a diverse, inclusive organization filled with both students wanting to find a h

name: Association of Latin American Students
description: The mission of the Association of Latin American Students (ALAS) is to create a Latin American community and provide support for people being away from home, especially for incoming grad students. Trying to connect with different cultures and creating bonds with them, socializing about the different and common things between them. The group maintains regular social gatherings including weekly sports events such as volleyball or soccer games.

name: Astronomy Club
description: The Astronomy Club is designed for anyone with an interest in astronomy, be it observational astronomy, or just a desire to ponder the big questions of the cosmos. The club aims to make good use of university facilities such as the Mees Observatory to give everyone an opportunity to experience the night sky in a new way. The club also utilizes its own array of telescopes on campus and promotes naked eye stargazing. name: ATHS Undergraduate Council
description: Our mission is to provide guidance, mentorship, and community for incoming ATHS (Archaeology, Technology, and Historical Structures) students and a support system for majors and minors throughout their undergraduate experience at University of Rochester. Our organization also strives to create a space for undergraduate students to connect with their peers, professors, and professionals in the field.

name: Audio Engineering Society
description: The Audio Engineering Society's mission is to promote the science and practice of audio by bringing students, faculty, alumni, leaders of the industry, and ideas together.

name: Aviation in Rochester
description: AIR aims to educate U of R students about aviation and expose them to unique aerodynamic experiences.

name: Badminton
description: UR Badminton is a sports club providing a space for players of all levels to engage in the sport of badminton. We provide a relaxed training atmosphere for those interested in recreational playing as well as for advanced players that want to compete in matches and tournaments.

name: Baja SAE
description: WHO WE ARE The UR Baja SAE team is a student-run, non-profit organization which designs, fabricates, tests, and competes with a single-seater off-road vehicle. From mechanical and biomedical engineering to optics and business majors, our numbers include anyone who is interested in learning design! Whether you have built a car from scratch or have never touched a wrench in your life, we will utilize any your experience and will teach you designing, manufacturing, and testing methods.

name: Baking Club
description: Our goal is to provide a space for students to explore their love of baking and expand their knowledge in the kitchen. We wish to give a creative outlet to those who need a break from the fast moving pace of the academic rigor of the UofR, especially for those without access to baking supplies or a kitchen. Join to meet people with similar interests and bond over the love of baking as well as explore other cultures!

name: Ballet Performance Group
description: The Ballet Performance Group at University of Rochester aims to provide an outlet for individuals who seek to learn and perform all styles of dance while encouraging an awareness and appreciation of classical ballet. Our group's foremost goal is to keep ballet technique alive on campus by using it as a foundation for all of the styles we perform. We welcome all levels of experience and offer dances that challenge and enhance the diverse abilities of our members. Every year, we put together two shows composed of classical ballet and student-choreographed pieces. We also perform as guest groups

name: Barbara J. Burger iZone
description: At iZone, we provide robust programming and services to students interested in developing their skills as creative problem solvers, innovators, and changemakers through credit-bearing courses and workshops, peer-led consulting services, and innovative events that help students hone various college competencies.

name: BCS & Neuroscience Undergraduate Council
description: The BCS & Neuroscience Undergraduate Council aims to connect BCS & Neuroscience students with professors and regularly pass on information about research opportunities, speakers, and more!

name: Best Buddies
description: Best Buddies International is an organization dedicated to ending social, physical, and economic isolation of people with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD). The organization works to establish a global volunteer movement that creates opportunities for meaningful and long-lasting one-to-one friendships, integrated employment, leadership development, and inclusive living for individuals with IDD. name: Bhangra
description: Over the past few years, Rochester Bhangra has established itself as a respected collegiate team, and we are known across the circuit for our unique style, as well as our unparalleled diversity. We aim to share and represent the culture and heart of Punjab through the camaraderie of our team, and strive to inspire everyone we perform for. name: Biomedical Engineering Society
description: The goal of BMES is to "promote the profession of Biomedical Engineering through study, research and discussion of the fields of Biomedical Engineering." The BMES encourages student interaction and collaboration and allows the students to come together under a common banner. Our university chapter is also a great place for discussion of issues that a Biomedical Engineering student may have. The University of Rochester BMES is active in hosting a wide variety of academic, social, mentoring, and career focused events. Past events have included internship and post-undergrad panels, student/facult

name: Birding Club
description: Our club's mission is to promote the education, observation, and appreciation of wildlife with a focus on birds and related conservation efforts. Through fun activities that involve birding around the state and community outreach, our club will provide an open and inclusive atmosphere that will allow all members of the campus community to engage with the natural world that surrounds them.

name: Black Student Athlete Coalition
description: The Black Student Athletic Coalition’s (B.S.A.C) purpose is to advocate for and support black student-athletes academically, mentally, and socially. Our goal is to establish a safe space for Black athletes on the University of Rochester (UofR) campus. Additionally, we seek to ensure athletic staff and all student-athletes are trained in cultural awareness to create a safe and collaborative environment for all. description: We, the students of the Black Students' Union (BSU) at the University of Rochester was founded upon the intent to promote social and cultural awareness, to foster diversification, and develop community relations within the University. name: Blue Dot Society
description: Blue Dot Society aims to discuss thought-provoking questions surrounding astrobiology. We hope to provide a space where students interested in astrobiology can come together to connect, engage in thoughtful discussion, learn, and have fun.

name: Book Club
description: Our organization strives to provide a space for students to discuss and explore their love of reading.

name: Brazilian Student Association
description: BRASA aims to foster the Brazilian community on campus, as well as to celebrate the Brazilian culture and raise awareness on issues that the country currently faces.

name: Campus Times
description: The Campus Times strives to report and analyze the events and issues that affect the UR community, offer an open forum for the expression of opinions, and provide students with opportunities to better their writing, reporting, and design skills through journalism. http://www.campustimes.org

name: Car Club
description: The student section of the University of Rochester Car Club will promote and create a respectful environment for students to share their knowledge, passions, and imaginations about everything car related. Students will discuss their interests, questions, and observations pertaining to vehicles at meetings and events.

name: Cards Club
description: The purpose of Cards Club is to engage the campus community in all activities and games regarding the usage of playing cards. Cards Club will strive to accomplish this by creating an enjoyable, inclusive environment for all participants to engage with one another, regardless of prior experiences or knowledge.

name: Carillon Guild
description: The mission of the Carillon Guild is to promote student leadership among the students who play the Hopeman Carillon. We wish to encourage students to plan activities, as well as have more experienced students teach the new ones.

name: Catan Club
description: Our mission is to provide regular, low-pressure opportunities for students to explore the shared pastime of playing Catan for enjoyment, skill-building, and community.

name: Catholic Newman Community
description: The mission of the Catholic Newman Community at the University of Rochester is to provide a welcoming family, in a collaborative and inclusive interfaith environment, for students and the larger University of Rochester community. Newman seeks to promote strong faith formation through the sacraments, education, service, and social programming.

name: Celtic
description: We are the University of Rochester's Irish Dance club! UR Celtic was formed in 2007 by two champion Irish Dancers in an effort to spread Irish culture at the University of Rochester. We teach and perform both traditional and modern Irish dance to all levels of dancers. In the fall, we compete at the Villanova Intercollegiate Irish Dance Festival, and in the spring we have our annual showcase. We also perform at various campus events, like Celebrate Diversity, the InspireDANCE Festival, for St. Patrick's Day, at charities and fundraisers, and with other dance groups. name: Center for Advising Services
description: The Center for Advising Services (CAS) supports undergraduate students with academic planning, problem-solving, and connecting with campus resources in a supportive and confidential environment. name: Center for Community Engagement
description: The Center for Community Engagement fosters collaborative leadership among students, the University, and community partners to discover transformative solutions and create equitable social change.

name: Center for Education Abroad
description: The Center for Education Abroad believes that education abroad is an integral part of the University experience. Through thoughtful planning and community support, we help students—in any major—conduct study abroad.

name: Chabad House
description: The purpose of Chabad House is to promote the awareness of the Jewish cultural and spiritual heritage, its values and traditions; and to facilitate the observance and study of traditional Judaism amongst the members of the University of Rochester Community. Chabad House promotes the Jewish Mystical Doctrine that each and every positive action has inherent value and helps make the entire world a better place.

name: Charles Drew Pre-Health Society
description: The Charles Drew Pre-Health Society is devoted to raising awareness on the University of Rochester campus and in the Rochester community about all issues related to healthcare and the health professions. We offer educational opportunities and speakers, community outreach and community service activities, and foster mentorship among students.

name: Chess Club
description: To provide an opportunity for students and faculty to play chess at both casual and competitive levels.

name: Chi Omega
description: Chi Omega is an intergenerational women's organization committed to our founding purposes: friendship, personal integrity, service to others, academic excellence and intellectual pursuits, community and campus involvement and personal and career development. We are sisters inspired by our values who serve the world while keeping Chi Omega ever at heart.

name: Chi Phi
description: To build better men through lifelong friendships, leadership opportunities, and character development.

name: Chinese Students and Scholars Association
description: CSSA is a student organization dedicated to serving all undergraduate Chinese students by providing academic and career support tailored to the unique challenges Chinese students face.

name: Club Baseball
description: We aim to provide club members with a fun, inclusive, and competitive environment to play baseball and foster the development of leadership, communication, and team skills.

name: Club Field Hockey
description: Our mission is to provide a fun, casual, and relaxed environment for all to play field hockey. We strive to be inclusive--we are a co-ed club and players of all levels of experience are welcome to join. Practices will focus on improving skills, running drills, and scrimmages. If you have any questions, email hwang50@u.rochester.edu

name: Club Softball
description: Our club softball team, the University of Rochester Stingers, is a group of passionate softball players from various backgrounds. While we enjoy competitive gameplay, our number one priority is making softball fun. We aim to create an inclusive environment for students to learn new skills and form lasting relationships with their teammates while improving their athletic skills and abilities.

name: Club Squash
description: Club Squash welcomes all undergraduate students who are interested in the game of squash. Regardless of skill level, gender, or class year you will be enthusiastically welcomed into the club. We split the club into two groups - those looking to play simply recreationally, and those looking to improve and challenge themselves. We look forward to seeing you on the courts!

name: Club Tennis
description: We are a co-ed, competitive, fun-loving tennis team! We hold practices 3 times a week, as well as participating in tournaments throughout the year. Besides tennis, we enjoy social events and hanging out with each other!

name: Coffee Club
description: Our mission is to foster a vibrant community of coffee enthusiasts dedicated to exploring the rich tapestry of local coffee culture in the Rochester area. We provide a welcoming space for members to savor diverse coffee offerings, embrace the city's unique character, and forge lasting connections.

name: College Democrats
description: The University of Rochester's chapter of College Democrats seeks to be an outlet for students to become civically engaged in both local and national politics. Through meaningful programming and community partnerships, we aim to encourage students to become advocates for democracy.

name: College Feminists
description: The purpose of the University of Rochester College Feminists is to educate the university community about comprehensive feminist issues to encourage activism on campus and beyond. In doing so, we discuss gender identity and gender-based issues, in the context of how gender intersects with race, culture, sexuality, and other marginalized experiences. We aim to enhance the campus community by raising awareness of intersectionality, inclusivity, diversity, and equity. name: College Republicans
description: Our mission is to define and discuss social problems, regulated by evidence and objectivity, recognizing that, in the pursuit of truth, all good faith parties are allies, political affiliation or party notwithstanding; to provide a setting for educative and productive discussion; to respect the rights of individuals party to such discussion; to host programs to the campus and greater Rochester community in furtherance of the principles supported by such discussions; and to connect our members with academic and political opportunities in accordance with such principles. name: Comics Club
description: Comics exists to foster an appreciation and understanding of comics of all time periods and cultures in addition to supporting the creation and publication of new comics. We seek to provide a place that supports comics creators, facilitates community among comics readers, and brings the medium of comics into the public eye. In doing so, we hope to bring together a diverse community of comic enthusiasts across the University of Rochester, the Eastman School of Music campuses, and the Greater Rochester Community.

name: Committee for Political Engagement
description: The Committee for Political Engagement (CPE), a Center For Community Engagement (CCE) initiative, is a non-partisan, student-led organization that promotes engagement in the civic process and domestic and international politics. CPE provides the University community with opportunities for voter registration, issue education, conferences, and more. In coordinating these efforts, CPE works closely with College Democrats and College Republicans, as well as other campus organizations.

name: Compeer Rochester
description: Through the power of human connection, Compeer serves as a bridge to better mental health and community integration for all. We envision a day when all communities embrace individuals and their families living with mental health challenges; when prevention begins early with children and their families; and when living, learning, working, and volunteering in the community is given expression through the social inclusion of all individuals and supported by the power of human connection and hope.

name: Computer Interest Floor
description: CIF is an interesting group of people whose interests and activities are as diverse as our members. While we go back to 1982, we’re just as dedicated to the university community as when we were providing some of the few computing resources on campus. Please visit our website (cif.rochester.edu) to learn more about what we do and apply to be a member! CIF provides several services to the University of Rochester and the community at large, including free 24-hour technical support, web hosting, Unix accounts, and a computer lab available to all University students with Windows, Mac, and Linux mac

name: Computer Science Undergraduate Council
description: The purpose of CSUG is to promote collaboration and a sense of community among not only the students of the Computer Science department, but also members of the University at large. The Council focuses on issues that relate to the field of Computer Science, specifically, including social and academic concerns.

name: Consulting Club
description: The Consulting Club is an organization for those interested in the consulting industry. The club is a welcoming community which hosts events every few weeks to educate students on the industry, and it especially focus on practice group case interviews, where students can gain experience on cases with their peers.

name: CRANES
description: Our mission is to bring light to cancer patients. We aim to do this through volunteering, fundraising to support research, families battling cancer, and healthcare institutions, while raising awareness on our campus community.

name: Creative Arts Club
description: We strive to strengthen the art community on the University of Rochester campus by providing an equipped studio space and conducting various activities inside and outside of the studio.

name: Cricket Club
description: The cricket club aims to bring all students together by playing tennis ball cricket on campus. All levels would be welcome including students who have never played the sport and want to learn to those who play recreationally and those who played competitively and want to engage in matches. This club aims to introduce and spread knowledge of cricket and encourages engagement from the student community.

name: Cru

name: David T. Kearns Center for Leadership and Student Success
Delta Kappa Epsilon
description: The objects of Delta Kappa Epsilon are the cultivation of general literature and social culture, the advancement and encouragement of intellectual excellence, the promotion of honorable friendship and useful citizenship, the development of a spirit of tolerance and respect for the rights and views of others, the maintenance of gentlemanly dignity, self-respect, and morality in all circumstances, and the union of stout hearts and kindred interests to secure to merit its due reward.

name: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc.
description: Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated is an organization of college educated women committed to the constructive development of its members and to public service with a primary focus on the Black community.

name: Delta Upsilon
description: Through the ties of friendship and brotherhood, Delta Upsilon exists to develop men who exemplify and uphold the values of leadership, diversity, and justice, and to sharpen and direct their talents for the benefit of the group, the individual, and the community.

name: Dominican Student Awareness (Quisqueya)
description: The Dominican Student Association (Quisqueya) exists to create a supportive community for students of Dominican heritage and those interested in Dominican culture. Our mission is to celebrate and share Dominican traditions, history, and values with the entire University of Rochester campus through cultural, educational, and social programming.

name: Douglass Leadership House
description: Named after Rochester icon Frederick Douglass, the mission of the Douglass Leadership House (DLH) is to establish an engaging intellectual community where students of all cultural backgrounds can come together and raise awareness of the many facets of the black experience; including culture, politics, history, and diasporic roots.

name: Drama House
description: Drama House’s goal is to create and promote a vibrant, educational, and student driven performing arts community on campus. Our members endeavor to do this by producing original workshops and lectures, providing a financially feasible rehearsal and performance space for student events, and building a home for artistically minded students to collaborate. Since its inception in 1971, Drama House has stood for our principles of creativity, artistic collaboration, and gender and sexuality inclusion. name: East Pen Pal Program
description: The East Pen Pal Program gives undergraduates the opportunity to correspond weekly with eighth graders from the East Lower School and participate in annual Pen Pal visit days.

name: EcoReps
description: By giving the EcoReps the skills and knowledge needed to promote environmentally responsible behavior in first-year residence halls, our program strives to create an environmentally literate student population.

name: Engineers Without Borders
description: The University of Rochester Chapter of Engineers Without Borders (EWB-UR) seeks to partner with developing communities worldwide in order to improve their quality of life through the design and implementation of sustainable engineering projects. We provide an environment for students to apply their academic skills to real world problems in an internationally responsible and globally beneficial way. Our vision is a world in which all communities have the capacity to meet their basic human needs.

name: Equestrian
description: We are a group of riders with backgrounds of all skill levels. Our love for riding brings us together and allows us to push ourselves to new limits, strengthen the bond between horse and rider, and build a community of fun, friendship, and respect.

name: ESM Asian Students' International Association

name: ESM EmpowHER
description: This organization focuses on the rights and needs of female-identifying students of all races and identities. Our events and communication draw attention to power dynamics that adversely affect female identifying students. We hope to create a safe community of Eastman students educated on social issues relevant to female-identifying individuals in order to optimize the learning environment for all students. EmpowHer hopes to equip all students with valuable tools to enter the music industry.

name: ESM George Walker Center
description: The Eastman School of Music is committed to: - Diversity, equity, and inclusion and strives for continuous improvement; fostering a community of musicians of diverse backgrounds and origins by creating an educational experience that is musically, socially and intellectually diverse; - Assuring that every person in our community is unquestionably welcome, safe, respected, and appreciated; and - Creating and encouraging an inclusive community that enriches the lives of our students, our faculty, our immediate community, and the world of music at large.

name: ESM Sibley Music Library

Grassroots strives to make an impact both on and off campus. name: Hillel
description: UR Hillel is proud to be the catalyst for vibrant, pluralistic, inclusive Jewish life at the University of Rochester. We embrace the core Jewish value of hachnasat orchim (welcoming all), with great spirit and energy. We connect students with one another, and with Jewish culture and traditions through religious life and celebrations, learning, civic engagement and social action, Israel, community and social connections, and leadership programs. HSA provides a welcoming space for Hindu students to connect, celebrate, and explore their traditions through festivals, temple visits, and meaningful dialogue. description: URIMPS is an all inclusive organization that will focuses on street and stage performance magic but discusses other types as well. This allows everyone to have their own style of performance.

name: Improv Club
description: The Improv Club is dedicated to creating a home for students of all backgrounds who are interested in improvisational comedy. We seek to be an all-inclusive group and to bolster the confidence and public speaking skills of members through performances and weekly public workshops.

description: Indulgence Dance Crew aims at promoting hip-hop culture through dance and creating space for hip-hop related interests to bond and grow at the University of Rochester.

description: The purpose of Japanese Students' Association is to provide a place within the University of Rochester student body where Japanese culture and language can be expressed and shared. Non-speakers and speakers alike can all find a niche in this group and enjoy what it has to offer. We fight for a world where the equal rights and humanity of both Palestinians and Israelis are recognized, from the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea. We aim to bring this vision to the University of Rochester.

JUR serves as a forum for the presentation of original research thereby encouraging the pursuit of significant scholarly endeavors. Seeking to enhance the scholarly community on campus, JUR also reflects students' varied interests.

We aim to form bridges between currently enrolled students and U of R alumni, between Korean companies and students interested in or planning to work in Korea, between students who are preparing to or currently are studying abroad in Korea and local students studying in Korea, and between transfer/exchange students from Korea and current URochester students.

Our KSU members represent the diverse multicultural community at the University of Rochester. name: Pet Rock Sketch Comedy
description: Pet Rock Sketch Comedy aims to provide an opportunity for students to explore, write, and perform completely student-run (and hopefully hilarious) sketch comedy for the entire University of Rochester Community. Through this club, we hope to create a space where people can expand their comedy knowledge, try out new forms of collaboration, and perform their own jokes for their friends in semester showcases.

name: Phoenix Fire
description: Phoenix Fire is dedicated to showcasing Classical Chinese dance and promoting cultural diversity on campus. We provide opportunities for everyone to explore, learn and perform Classical Chinese dance while hoping to inspire the understanding and appreciation of it. We welcome those with any level of experience, and members can choose their own piece of interest for their performance repertoire. There will be tutors to facilitate the practices every week and we will work together to enjoy the performances and the annual showcase.

name: Photography
description: UR Photography Club is for all students interested in photography to learn, create, critique, and share images. We welcome photographers of all skill levels and provide a variety of events for them to practice taking pictures, and opportunities to network and learn from other photographers. UR Photography's squad of experienced photographers is available to take pictures at your event! If you are an organization and want to hire us for event photos, please contact us using our email below.

name: Physics and Astronomical Sciences Student Association for Graduate Engagement
Pokémon Club
description: Our organization aims to provide a shared, inclusive space for everyone to immerse themselves in all things Pokémon. We are dedicated to ensuring that all members feel included, whether they are newcomers or longtime fans.

name: Polish Students' Association
description: Promote an awareness and understanding of Polish culture, history, and heritage to any individuals at the University of Rochester. Promote an appreciation of Polish culture and heritage as it exists on campus and in the world community. Provide learning opportunities for the UR community with respect to the Polish culture, history, and language.

name: Postdoctoral Association
description: The Postdoctoral Association (PDA) provides career development, networking opportunities, and professional recognition specifically for postdoctoral appointees. Through these efforts, we hope to contribute to the professional advancement of postdoctoral appointees and highlight our contributions to scientific research at the University of Rochester.

name: Pre-Dental Club
description: The Pre-dental Club at the University of Rochester will be dedicated to supporting and providing pre-dental students with the resources they need in order to be successful in their academics as well as providing the volunteering, shadowing, and research opportunities necessary to have a well-rounded dental school application. The pre-dental club focuses on bringing more awareness to dentistry as a possible pre-health field at the University of Rochester curriculum for students to become interested in and get into. Professionals in Dentistry have often times lacked overall diversity thus, raisi

name: Pre-Law Society
description: The University of Rochester Pre-Law Society is established for the purpose of providing undergraduate students with the opportunity to learn about law school and its associated admissions process. In addition, the University of Rochester Pre-Law Society aims to encourage undergraduates to learn more about legal processes and professions.

name: Pre-Physician Assistant Society
description: We strive to inform and prepare students pursuing a career as a Physician Assistant by providing education, resources, and community.

name: Protestant Chapel Community
description: The Protestant Chapel Community (PCC) is a ministry of Genesee Area Campus Ministries (hereinafter) and is led by a student Steering Committee and a Chaplain who is an ordained Protestant minister and the Director of GACM. PCC is a gathering of Christians and interfaith neighbors from many spiritual backgrounds working together to serve God in the University and beyond. PCC provides a place for Christian worship, silly fun, service, and the contemplative study of scripture. We welcome a diversity of traditions and viewpoints while celebrating the progressive nature of Christ's teachings. We ho

name: Psi Upsilon
description: United in Friendship, Psi Upsilon members aspire to moral, intellectual and social excellence in themselves as they seek to inspire these values in society.

name: Quantitative Finance Group
description: The Quantitative Finance Club empowers students to explore the intersection of finance, mathematics, and technology. Our mission is to provide a platform for members to deepen their understanding of quantitative finance through collaborative learning, real-world applications, and problem-solving.

name: Queer in Color
description: Queer in Color is an organization that is not only a safe space for students but is meant to take action for the discussions hosted. Through workshops, we will teach students about important topics including but not limited to health, professional life, and personal/social life. We also make an effort to celebrate queer joy!

name: Quiz Bowl
description: As the Quiz Bowl group at the University of Rochester, we aim to provide a space to play academic trivia games. The topics covered include history, music, philosophy, pop culture, science, and everything in between. We also compete at tournaments hosted by other universities in the region.

name: Rangoli
description: Rochester Rangoli, a South Asian performance group, strives to explore the culture of South Asian countries through dance! This all-embracing dance form bridges the gap between Eastern and Western styles. We hope to provide our members with an inclusive and judgement-free environment where students of all levels of experience can learn South Asian dance segments. Our group aims to cater to the busy schedules of most UR students by allowing flexibility while still preparing for numerous performances to showcase South Asian dance.

name: Red Cross
description: Guided by the fundamental principles of the American Red Cross and its mission to prevent and alleviate human suffering in the face of emergencies by mobilizing the power of volunteers and the generosity of donors the UR Red Cross Club, will learn, practice and exemplify humanitarian values through mission-related service projects. The service projects will focus on preparedness, blood, and fundraising. UR Red Cross seeks to be a place where anyone, regardless of their background, is encouraged to join this nationwide and international humanitarian service and can stand united to help a greate

name: Refugee Student Alliance
description: Since 2009, we've offered multiple volunteer opportunities for University of Rochester students and staff to foster community relations. Specifically, we've volunteered at and worked with Refugees Helping Refugees (http://rhrroc.org), Mary's Place (http://www.marysplaceoutreach.org), and Rochester Refugee Resettlement Services (https://www.rochesterrefugeeservices.org). We strongly encourage and invite you to participate in these volunteering efforts!

name: Religious & Spiritual Life
description: Religious & Spiritual Life is a place for people to worship in their particular faith and a place where people of different faiths, or no religious tradition at all, can share in dialogue, worship, and interfaith education. Our multi-faith community and our interfaith engagements contribute significantly to the rich diversity that is the University of Rochester experience.

name: Residence Hall Association
description: The Residence Hall Association empowers residents through leadership, collaboration, advocacy, and recognition by serving as a platform for enacting change within the residential community.

name: ResLife - D'Lions
description: Organization designated to assisting first-years transition to living on campus through creating a welcoming hall community alongside a first-year team and constructing programs for residents, while also working to promote campus spirit and community service.

name: RICE Crew
description: RICE (Rochester International Choreography Entertainment) Crew, a performance group, promotes the cultural aspects of Korean pop dance (Kpop) and music while integrating it with its American hip hop counterparts. We hope to promote the similarities and link between the two genres. RICE Crew performs in many campus organizations' events as illustration of Korean pop, dance, and music. Anyone who is interested in learning Korean and American hip hop dances are welcomed regardless of ethnicity. Instagram: @ricecrewofficial

name: River Campus Libraries
description: Provide expertise, collections, experiential learning, and spaces that spark curiosity, fuel contemplation, connect ideas, and empower experimentation that makes the world ever better.

name: River Campus Medical Emergency Response Team
description: The University of Rochester River Campus Medical Emergency Response Team is committed to providing quality care to the University community. MERT works together with the Department of Public Safety to respond to medical emergencies on the River Campus. MERT works with University Health Services to ensure that all members are highly trained and providing high quality care as well as having the proper equipment to respond to medical emergencies.

name: Robotics Club
description: An organization for coordinating, supporting, and housing competitive and non-competitive student-led robotics projects. We also aim to educate members in robotics-related tools and techniques useful for these projects such as programming, computer-aided design, 3D printing, robotics algorithms, and embedded systems techniques.

name: ROC Players
description: ROC Players strives to provide opportunities for students to learn about, participate in, and lead any aspect of a high caliber, completely student-run, full musical theatre production for the entire University of Rochester community. Through this, we enhance and expand the University's theatrical community as well as enjoy the process of putting on a musical.

name: Rochester Design Hub
description: RDH is a community for students interested in design. Through hands-on projects, events, and professional development, we help students explore fields like product, UX, and graphic design to build skills and portfolio experience.

name: Rochester Indian Association
description: RIA was formed, in the spring of 2007. It is intended to serve as a platform for general social mingling and interpersonal interactions among students of Indian origin in the University of Rochester. RIA aims to foster our cultural bindings and encourage oneness on this campus by creating an ensemble of all graduate, post-doctoral and under-graduate students as a well knit community. For this purpose, RIA handles various affairs of a social nature such as Diwali Dhamaka, Holi Night, Independence Day celebrations and many more. In addition, we do our best to ensure a smooth transition in the li

name: Rochester Outdoor Cycling Club
description: Many students at the university choose cycling as a healthy mode of transportation that effectively boosts cardiovascular fitness. The University of Rochester Cycling Club is dedicated to encouraging students to enjoy scenic rides, stay active, and learn bicycle repair and customization skills through club activities, fostering a healthy lifestyle and practical expertise.

name: Rochester Producers & Musicians
description: Rochester Producers & Musicians (RPM) is an organization by musical artists, for musical artists. Our goal is to foster a diverse community for students interested in independent music creation and performance organization. We hope to serve as an accommodating vessel providing opportunities for students to network and collaborate, emulating the music industry on a miniature scale.

name: Rock Climbing
description: The Rock Climbing club's mission is to promote the sport of rock climbing at the University of Rochester. We seek to grow a community of climbers who engage in and appreciate the sport by bringing together experienced and inexperienced rock climbers within the community. Within this community, we aim to develop and maintain a strong competitive team able to consistently compete at the highest level.

name: Rocketry Club
description: The University of Rochester Rocketry Club is committed to advancing student engagement in aerospace engineering through hands on participation in the NASA Student Launch competition in Huntsville, Alabama. Our mission is to design, build, and launch a high powered rocket by collaboration across disciplines such as avionics, electronics, 3D modeling, and structural engineering. We strive to inspire and educate students, empowering them to pursue their passion for rocketry and space exploration.

name: ROCTalks
description: ROCTalks aims to make unique voices heard through changing the sphere of public speaking and speaking louder for issues and ideas that we are passionate about, to the university’s diverse audience and the rest of the modern world.

name: Rotaract
description: The mission of Rotaract is to provide an opportunity for students to enhance the knowledge and skills that will assist them in personal development, to address the physical and social needs of their communities, and to promote better relations between all people worldwide through a framework of friendship and service.

name: Roundnet
description: The purpose of UR Roundnet is to gather members of the entire University of Rochester community who have an interest in playing roundnet. This includes but is not limited to all undergraduate and graduate students. As such, a group will be built with two core intentions: (1) foster an appreciation for the sport on campus and (2) improve skills in order to compete at the club intercollegiate level and Spikeball Roundnet Association sanctioned events.

name: Royals Dance Team
description: As a team, we strive to bring the campus together through dance and spirit, mainly through performances at sporting events for varsity basketball teams and club ice hockey, and our end-of-semester showcase. We create a space for dancers of all levels to express their spirit, pride, and energy through movement, as well as a space for team creativity and contribution to group choreography. We strive to unify our team through the various skills and strengths of our members.

name: Running Club
description: The purpose of URunning Club is to provide a fun and healthy environment for undergraduates. students, graduate students, and faculty members to run both competitively and non-competitively. URunning Club will inform its members of safe running procedures and proper training techniques during club meetings and training sessions. URunning Club will also encourage social interactions among the University of Rochester community, and will act to integrate the running community of the Rochester area and other universities We explore the parks surrounding UR on our runs, in addition to the city itse

name: Sailing
description: The mission of the UR Sailing Club is to foster an interest in sailing at the university and support marine safety through education and experience. We travel to compete against other sailing teams in MAISA and ICSA and hold practices every week.

name: SALSEROS
description: The purpose of S.A.L.S.E.R.O.S. at the University of Rochester is to provide cultural and social expression through the art of dance among our fellow community members and to educate the university community about Spanish and Latino culture.

name: SAS|Hajim Graduate Education and Postdoctoral Affairs
description: The SAS|Hajim Graduate Education and Postdoctoral Affairs (GEPA) office strives to enrich the experience of graduate students and postdoctoral scholars by working with graduate programs and campus partners to build and maintain an engaged research and learning community. This is achieved through social and professional programming and by supporting faculty and staff who work with graduate students and postdoctoral scholars.

name: Scribbling Society
description: Scribbling Society provides a space for fiction writers to develop their craft and receive feedback. We are a collaborative club where writers of all skill levels can find a community and joy in writing.

name: Senior Giving Campaign
description: The mission of the advisory board is to promote philanthropy and philanthropic education to URochester students, and support the Senior Giving Committee.

name: SFI
description: To celebrate and promote Israeli culture, history, and peoples through a variety of venues and programs

name: She's The First
description: She's The First at the University of Rochester aims to sponsor girls education in low income countries, allowing them to become the first in their families to graduate from secondary school. We achieve this through both fundraising efforts, as well as events to raise awareness about the issue of poverty and education for women. This chapter is part of a larger national organization: She's The First. In addition, our chapter hopes to accomplish additional work with girls in the local Rochester community, such as regular tutoring events and after-school activities.

name: Sigma Alpha Iota
description: Our mission is to encourage, nurture, and support the art of music. We will - Support and encourage women musicians of all ages, races and nationalities - Support and promote successful and innovative educational programs for all stages of life - Cultivate excellence in musical performance - Promote programs and activities that stress the love and importance of music in our lives - Recognize the technological advancements in the field of music - Dedicate financial resources that ensure the continuation of programs necessary to support the objectives of the fraternity in perpetuity - Have, as m

name: Sigma Chi
description: Sigma Chi aims to be the preeminent leadership development fraternity in the greek letter world, encouraging brothers to live by our values of friendship, justice and learning.

name: Sigma Delta Tau
description: Sigma Delta Tau empowers each member to reach her fullest potential by enriching the experience of women with similar ideals, building lasting relationships, promoting civic responsibility and fostering personal growth.

name: Sigma Phi Epsilon
description: SigEp is redefining fraternity on college campuses across the country. We complement a man’s education by delivering a premier student experience in one of the most formative times of his life. Through SigEp, men strengthen their character, build leadership and interpersonal skills, and learn to develop healthy, lifelong relationships that are essential to a successful and fulfilling life. SigEp was founded with the Cardinal Principles of Virtue, Diligence and Brotherly Love. Our mission is “Building Balanced Men,” which is achieved through a commitment to Sound Mind and Sound Body.

name: Sigma Psi Zeta Sorority, Inc.
description: Sigma Psi Zeta is a progressive, multicultural, and social Greek Organization known for its history of Asian and Asian-American advocacy. Since our founding, Sigma Psi Zeta's mission has been to empower women of all ethnicity and backgrounds. Our founding values are further exemplified by our National Philanthropy: Combating Violence Against Women in all forms and across all cultures.

name: Sihir Bellydance Ensemble
description: Our main mission is to spread cultural awareness and body positivity throughout the campus and community setting. We help to achieve this mission by providing a positive, inclusive environment that encourages every member to learn bellydance, along with the surrounding culture. Sihir puts on a semesterly performance as well as guest performs for other club and community events. All of our performances allow us to spread our love for bellydance, the surrounding culture, and our body positive message within the University of Rochester and the Rochester community.

name: Simulation Gaming Association
description: The goal of the University of Rochester Simulation Gaming Association is to provide University of Rochester students and members of the Rochester community with an open community for the discussion and furthering of interests in simulation gaming, tabletop gaming, and derivative activities — including, but not limited to, board gaming, tabletop roleplaying, and trading/collectable card games —, conducting social events to expand and develop this community, and promoting simulation gaming to the community as a whole. Board Game meetings are Mondays from 7-11pm in Douglass 401. TTRPG meetings ar

name: SMD Entrepreneurs
description: SMD Entrepreneurs will provide a platform for entrepreneurial minded trainees to explore developing a business based on their interests. We will provide many resources including connecting with entrepreneurial leaders in the finger lakes and western, NY regions as well as esteemed UR alumni all over the country. We will provide ample opportunities to practice pitches and get feedback on business model development. name: Society for Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science (SACNAS)
Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers
description: The Society of Asian Scientists and Engineers aims to increase positive visible impact and diversity of Asian heritage scientists and engineers on campus, to build a bridge between the university and employers for the networking possibilities and business connections, and to give back to the Rochester community. Our mission is to create a place for other people to learn and connect culturally, and to support its students, not only academically and professionally, but also in individual growth and development.

name: Society of Earth Science Students
description: Our mission in SESS is to bring together students who are enthusiastic about the environmental sciences, earth sciences, and geosciences. We aim to foster a strong community where our students can bond over similar passions while expanding their academic and professional networks. SESS intents to expose students to the earth and environmental sciences outside the classroom through seminars, guest speakers in related fields, educational field trips, group discussions, and other social events. We plan to inform students about career paths after college, prepare them for graduate school, and prov

name: Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers
description: SHPE promotes the development of Hispanics in engineering, science and other technical professions to achieve educational excellence, economic opportunity and social equity. We are brought together by heritage, social responsibility and desire to improve the equality of all people through the use of science and technology. We value excellence in education, professional pursuits and leadership. We obtain excellence through integrity, empowerment, achievement, diversity and continuous improvement.

name: Society of Physics Students
description: The University of Rochester chapter of the National Society of Physics Students is dedicated to supporting students in their study of physics and to ameliorating the appreciation of science by the University community and the public. On campus we facilitate group projects and social activities amongst physics students as well as providing free tutoring for all physics classes. Off campus, our outreach program aims to share our enthusiasm for physics with students in the Rochester area.

name: Society of Undergraduate Biology Students
description: Our purpose is to promote faculty-student interaction, to serve as a guiding force for Biology majors/interests, provide networking opportunities through events, and to cater to the needs of the membership through member input.

name: Society of Undergraduate Public Health Students
description: The Society of Undergraduate Public Health Students is devoted to connecting those with a common interest in public health. We aim to bridge the gap between the various disciplines in public health and to create public health opportunities by fostering connections between students, faculty, and the community. In addition, we aim to educate the student body about issues in public health through our events.

name: Society of Undergraduate Statistics Students
description: SUSS works to spread interest about statistics on campus among students through varying promotional events, fundraisers, co-sponsorships. Help statistics students with classes, career opportunities, advising, and build a statistics community on campus.

name: Society of Women Engineers
description: The Society of Women Engineers is an organization that empowers women to succeed and advance in the field of engineering. Our aim is to build leadership skills, provide networking opportunities, and instill a strong sense of mutual support and community.

name: Society of Women in Astronomy and Physics
description: SWAP aims to improve recruitment and retention rates for gender minorities in physics, especially women, throughout the university and local community.

name: Solar Splash
description: University of Rochester Solar Splash is a group of students who are committed to designing, building, and racing a solar-powered electric boat. Our group emphasizes learning and practicing engineering skills through hands-on construction and real-world application of theory learned in the classroom. Our goal is to learn a hands-on approach to the hydrodynamics, materials, mechanics, and electronics involved in building an electric boat to enter the international Solar Splash Competition each year. Through extensive drafting, construction, and testing, we hope to achieve success as a team while

name: Spanish and Latino Students' Association
description: We, the members of the Spanish and Latino Students' Association (S.A.L.S.A) at the University of Rochester, desire : To provide cultural, social, political, and educational awareness among our fellow members; to enlighten the University community about Spanish and Latino culture.

name: SPIE
description: The SPIE University of Rochester Student Chapter was founded in May 2009: a much-needed student organization that brings together graduate students with common interests in optics and/or imaging across the University. Inspired by the interdisciplinary nature of SPIE we have reached out to students from optics, biomedical engineering, physics, medical center, chemical engineering, and computer science. Our chapter currently has more than 70 members.

name: STEM Initiative
description: STEM Initiative aims to inspire students in Rochester elementary and middle schools to pursue studies and careers in the STEM fields. We hope to have a longlasting impact on these students to stimulate interest in the STEM field. We also hope to make STEM education more widely available to young students who currently lack access to the full spectrum of STEM education.

name: Strong Jugglers
description: The Strong Jugglers aim to promote a spirit of sharing in order to provide a climate for learning and performing juggling and other circus arts. Open club meetings are held Tuesdays and Thursdays. Our mission includes the following goals: A. To have fun. B. To teach all those members of the University community who are interested in juggling and the circus arts. C. To provide a safe environment free from breakables. D.
