name: Student Activities
description: Through partnerships with student employees and student leaders, our team strives to create a welcoming and inclusive community by engaging students in creative programming and traditions, meaningful employment, experiential learning opportunities, and innovative services and facilities.

name: Student Activities Board
description: The purpose of Student Activities Board shall be to provide varied and interesting entertainment for as many members of the University community as possible while aiding other campus organizations in their event planning process. Events shall include, but are not limited to speakers, musical performances, community weekend events, and other interactive activities. Factors for selecting these activities include, but are not limited to tradition, culture, community, and perceived enjoyment and value. While the Student Activites Board should collaborate with faculty, staff, alumni and other stude

name: Student Alumni Ambassadors
description: The Student Alumni Ambassadors are a select group of undergraduate students who serve as liaisons within the University alumni community, offering insights into current student culture and sharing their personal Rochester experience. The Student Alumni Ambassador program builds relationships among students and alumni and fosters pride in the University of Rochester.

name: Student Association for the Development of Arab Cultural Awareness
description: SADACA aims to foster an effective, fruitful, and inclusive environment for individuals interested in the Arab Region where they could meet and exchange ideas and increase awareness of pertinent issues perpetrating the Arab world both on the University of Rochester Campus and in the greater Rochester area.

name: Student Association of Vegan and Vegetarian Youth
description: Our goal is to help reduce animal suffering by increasing awareness of animal rights issues and the negative environmental impacts of a non-vegan diet. We also provide support for vegetarians, vegans, and anyone who is interested in learning about how our dietary and lifestyle choices affect animals, humans, and the environment.

name: Student National Association of Teachers of Singing
Student Organization for Caribbean Awareness
description: The purpose of the Student Organization for Caribbean Awareness (SOCA) is to promote and share the values and richness that are found among Caribbean nations. Through various cultural and social programs, SOCA works to create a community for Caribbean students which affirms their cultural traditions while simultaneously informing and educating the University community about the countries they represent. By sharing Caribbean culture, in its many forms, SOCA works to establish and maintain strong relationships with the University community, the Rochester community and the international community

name: Students for a Democratic Society
description: URochester SDS is an association of the student left at the University of Rochester. We aim to win a new society free of racism, sexism, heterosexism, classism, authoritarianism, war, and ecological devastation by instilling democratic values throughout campus. We seek to achieve a truly participatory society, consisting of liberatory institutions in all spheres of social life. Our structure and methods will embody the spirit of our democratic vision and work towards creating a better tomorrow.

name: Students' Association for Interfaith Cooperation
description: SAIC provides students a forum where they can share their spiritual beliefs and traditions and learn about those of others through dialogue, education and awareness, service, and social programs. It seems our campus community grows more diverse with every year, yet we are often hesitant to inquire about others' religious and cultural traditions, to ask how and why others are different from us. At SAIC, we believe our differences are just as beautiful as our similarities. We believe in having respectful dialogue, expressing our curiosity, and building bridges across lines of faith and culture,

name: Students' Association Government
description: The University of Rochester Students' Association Government is the undergraduate student governing body. We advocate on behalf of students to school administrators, we work on campus life and academic improvements to make students' lives at the University better, and we manage clubs and organizations on campus.

name: Sustainable Labs Initiative
description: The Sustainable Labs Initiative (SLI) is a grassroots community organization dedicated to fostering a culture of sustainability within research and clinical laboratories at the University of Rochester. By addressing the environmental impact of laboratory practices, we aim to foster eco-conscious research, reduce waste, enhance resource efficiency, and implement sustainable solutions to ensure a healthier planet.

name: Table Tennis
description: UR Table Tennis is dedicated to promoting the sport of table tennis at the University of Rochester. Focusing on recreational and competitive play, the club allows experienced players opportunities to sharpen their skills while providing casual players with a relaxed environment to learn or rally. URTT organizes on and off-campus scrimmages and competes in National Collegiate Table Tennis Association tournaments.

name: Tae Kwon Do
description: The purpose of the University of Rochester's Tae Kwon Do Club is to teach the art of Tae Kwon Do. This art will be taught with the goal of building an understanding of the unity of techniques, as well as the mind, body, and (indomitable fighting) spirit.

name: Taiwanese Student Association
description: TSA is a student organization at the University of Rochester, aimed to promote Taiwanese traditions, customs, and art forms through cultural events and showcases. We aim to provide a supportive and inclusive community where members feel a sense of belonging and camaraderie, fostered a deeper understanding and appreciation for cultural diversity among our members, whether you call Taiwan home or not.

name: Tau Beta Pi
description: The NY K Chapter of Tau Beta Pi aims to recognize engineering students who have distinguished themselves by their academic performance and exemplary character. Members of Tau Beta Pi will contribute to both the campus and city of Rochester community through co-sponsorship events, regular tutoring and volunteering on and off campus.

name: Team Green
description: The University of Rochester promotes a sustainable society through our education, research, patient care, and health programs, in the operation of our campuses and facilities, and in our interactions with the community. The Sustainability Office is the central hub for supporting and promoting these efforts toward a sustainable and equitable future.

name: The CubeSat Club
description: CubeSat is a student run engineering organization that is focused on designing and manufacturing miniature satellites to serve as a test-bed for low Earth Orbit scientific experiments, to develop new satellite technologies, and provide a robust educational experience for the next generation of engineers at the University of Rochester

name: The Health Outreach, Partnerships, Equity Alliance
description: Our mission is to empower passionate students to engage in public health equity initiatives at local, national, and global levels. Through forming partnerships with organizations, we strive to learn about evolving complex health challenges through volunteering, fundraising, and education.

name: The Learning Center
description: The Learning Center is a resource for undergraduate and graduate students looking to do their best academic work. Our office promotes quality learning, whether you’re looking for personalized coaching, collaborative study groups, or a quiet space to focus on your studying. We offer a range of programs that are all evidence-based and free.

name: The Liaison Project
description: The Liaison Project is a trainee-led organization within the School of Medicine and Dentistry (SMD) that provides graduate students, medical trainees, and postdoctoral fellows with the opportunity to practice the skills of Medical Science Liaisons (MSLs) and Medical Affairs professionals. Through structured clinical trial presentations, group discussions, and peer-to-peer scientific exchange, members will engage in real-world style dialogues that mirror the interactions between industry medical teams and healthcare professionals. The mission of this group is to uniquely position URMC trainees

name: The National Organization for the Professional Advancement of Black Chemists and Chemical Engineers
The Neurodiversity Alliance
description: The Neurodiversity Alliance’s mission is to improve the life of every person with a learning disability. We fulfill our mission by being part of a national, supportive and growing network of youth mentorship programs and student organizations run by and for those with learning differences, and by organizing advocates to support the full inclusion of people with learning disabilities and ADHD in all aspects of society.

name: The Opposite of People
description: To encourage vigorous participation in University life and a general advancement of the arts in the community, by the fostering and promotion of widespread dramatic literacy.

name: Thomistic Institute
description: The Thomistic Institute exists to promote Catholic truth in our contemporary world by strengthening the intellectual formation of Christians at universities, in the Church, and in the wider public square. The thought of St. Thomas Aquinas, the Universal Doctor of the Church, is our touchstone.

name: Title IX Office
description: The Title IX Office is committed to fostering a culture of prevention and awareness to end sexual violence, cultivate relationship respect, and create consent culture through education. Title IX is a federal civil rights law that prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex—including pregnancy and related conditions—in educational programs and activities. This can include sexual harassment, sexual assault, dating and domestic violence, and stalking in any educational, athletic, or other program or activity of a federally funded school, that jeopardizes a person's equal access to education. Her

name: Trebellious A Cappella
description: Trebellious is an all-gender a cappella group focused on expanding the a cappella community by teaching workshops open to all people at the University of Rochester. Our goal is to provide access to and education about a cappella music to anyone, regardless of experience level, and foster a community focused on the learning and love of music. To do so, we maintain a "teaching group" that is audition-based and holds separate rehearsals to be able to provide that musical education to our workshop.

name: Ukrainian Students' Association
description: Raise awareness and foster the understanding of Ukrainian culture to individuals at the University of Rochester. Provide educational opportunities for the university community, ensuring respect and acknowledgment of Ukrainian history, language, and heritage.

name: Undergraduate Anthropology Council
description: The purpose of the Undergraduate Anthropology Council (U.A.C.) is to promote a fuller understanding of the field of anthropology and related fields through interaction with students, faculty, and staff at the University of Rochester. U.A.C., by encouraging dialogue between students, faculty, and staff, hopes to emphasize the ways in which anthropological knowledge can enrich and broaden the perspective students to the many other fields of study offered at the University of Rochester.

name: Undergraduate Chemistry Society
description: We seek to maintain a group of students interested in chemistry and to foster that interest in these students and in the community at large. We do this via social, educational, and outreach events throughout the year. Tutoring offered: Monday, Genesee 325, 7:30-8:30 pm. Wednesday, Genesee 325, 8-9 pm.

name: Undergraduate English Council
description: We strive to foster community, connect students to resources, and encourage an appreciation of the humanities on campus. We aim to accomplish these goals through events, information settings, and visibility on campus. It is our goal to connect students, including but not limited to those who study English, to the opportunities and events offered at the University of Rochester ranging from internships and scholarships to classes and author visits.

name: Undergraduate Film Council
description: The purpose of UFC shall be to provide the University of Rochester community with a safe and creative space for fellow filmmakers, artists, and non artists of all kinds to enjoy the art of filmmaking. The council will provide workshops and opportunities for students to expand their filmmaking knowledge and experience.Students will learn, discuss, and practice all things film through workshops, discussions, and video projects. Each project will be allowed an entire semester to be made, where it will go through various stages of production.

name: Undergraduate Finance and Economics Council
description: The goal of FEC is to foster a friendly environment where students interested in Economics and Finance can network with each other and learn about great career opportunities. Also, we aim to better connect the students to the faculty, the University of Rochester alumni, and the professionals outside of the University. Through events with professionals, closer interaction with the economics department faculty, networking events and other programs, FEC provides a forum for students of any specialty interested in Economics, Business, and Finance.

name: Undergraduate History Council
description: The UHC is an organization by and for students interested in the study of history. We host events related to historical and historiographical topics and collaborate with the History Department to promote lectures, workshops, and panel discussions.

name: Undergraduate Philosophy Council
description: Philosophy Council is a relaxed club for students to share ideas, viewpoints, and perspectives about different philosophical concepts. We meet every Friday from 1:30 - 3 PM in the Philosophy/Linguistics lounge on the fifth floor of Lattimore Hall. Our discussions are open to all students from all majors and walks of life - we specifically design them to be accessible and assume no prior knowledge of philosophy.

name: UNICEF
description: The purpose of this organization is to organize students for the survival, protection and development of children worldwide through education, advocacy and fundraising as a UNICEF Campus Initiative group at the University of Rochester through the U.S. Fund for UNICEF.

name: University of Rochester Bee Campus Committee
description: URBCC is an Advisory Board whose purpose is to carry out the Xerces Society’s requirements for maintaining the Bee Campus USA designation at the University of Rochester. These requirements (listed at https://beecityusa.org/bee-campus-usa-commitments/) all aim towards advocating for the protection of pollinators. URBCC seeks to enact pollinator conservation on the University of Rochester campus to the best of our ability, engaging and educating the community with open access to information about the importance of pollinators to our temperate eastern deciduous forest ecosystem. name: University of Rochester Science Policy Initiative
description: Our mission is to empower students to engage with science policy by translating evidence into action, building policy literacy, and creating a campus community that connects research, ethics, and public decision-making.

name: University of Rochester Women in Neuroscience
Varsity Student Athlete Advisory Committee
description: The Varsity Student-Athlete Advisory Committee (VSAAC) empowers student-athletes to make a meaningful impact both on and off-campus by promoting and facilitating community outreach programs through volunteer opportunities. VSAAC represents the student-athlete voice in Division III governance by reviewing legislation, addressing significant student-athlete issues, implementing national initiatives, and fostering a deeper understanding of Division III while enhancing the overall student-athlete experience.

name: Video Game Dev Club
description: The Video Game Development Club aims to create a space that welcomes students to explore the world of video games and express themselves through participating in group and individual projects regardless of experience. The club encourages discussions of video games, ranging from video games as a product, or the art of creating video games.

name: Vietnamese Students Association
description: The VSA at the University of Rochester, as a cultural non-profit organization, serves to unify the Vietnamese population, embrace Vietnamese heritage and spread Vietnamese culture to the University of Rochester community. We host fun events to give everyone a taste of Vietnamese culture.

name: Vocal Point
description: The goal of Vocal Point is to contribute to the musical diversity at the University of Rochester and to generate an excitement for a cappella music. Vocal Point strive to hold up the musical integrity of the group in all of our actions, support the musical growth of the group as a whole, and promote various types of unaccompanied vocal music to the Rochester community and beyond. name: Water Polo
description: UR Water Polo is a coed student-run club sport. Made up of both undergraduates and graduates, the team normally practices twice a week and competes against other colleges in the New York Division of the Collegiate Water Polo Association. UR Water Polo aims to be inclusive, allowing students with no prior polo experience to join and learn about the sport, while also promoting intercollegiate competition. Usually, we practice Tuesdays and Thursdays from 8-9:30pm.

name: Women and Minorities in Computing
description: The UR Women and Minorities in Computing (WiC-MiC) aims to create a support network through mentorship, education, and resources for historically underrepresented minorities within the field of computer science. This network includes first-generation students, women, LGBTQIA+ students, and historically underrepresented racial groups (Black/African American, Hispanic/Latinx, Indigenous Peoples, and Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander), both at our institution and within the Greater Rochester community.

name: Women's Club Basketball
description: To empower and unite female identifying students who share a passion for basketball, and are looking for a fun and safe environment to share their competitive spirit.

name: Women's Club Soccer
description: The mission of the Women's Club Soccer team at the University of Rochester is to allow students the opportunity to play at a competitive level, while still having time to pursue other activities on campus. One of the main objectives of this club is to challenge members to excel on and off the field. It is required that all members attend practice, unless they have a valid excuse, or they will not be included in game rosters. name: Women's Club Volleyball
description: The purpose of the University of Rochester Women's Volleyball Club is to promote and develop the sport of volleyball among individuals at the University of Rochester, and to positively represent our school, the University of Rochester, in collegiate club league tournaments. We will accomplish this aim by: 1) Providing a suitable atmosphere for all members to play volleyball 2) Assisting all members interested in learning how to play the game of volleyball, working as a team to hone our skills and improve our gameplay, and assisting team members on our skills to improve them and gameplay 3) Com

name: Women's Leadership Alliance
description: To establish and develop sisterhood (by building strong and genuine relationships with other girls/women within the organization). To develop and maintain academic excellence (by consistently growing and showing effort in school/with academics) and to build mentorship partnerships (by maintaining strong relationships with mentors and/or mentees between middle/high school students and undergraduate/graduate/postgraduate women).

name: Women's Rugby
description: We are the UR Sledgehammers! We strive first and foremost to be awesome, to make a rugger out of everyone and finally to RUCK, MAUL, and SCRUM our way to victory! We want to spread the amazing and exhilarating sport of RUGBY to the campus community because big or small, tall or short, we can make a rugger out of anyone so come check us out! Absolutely no experience needed!

name: Women's Ultimate Frisbee
description: The Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club of the University of Rochester will develop their ultimate frisbee skills as a team and will teach others about ultimate frisbee. This organization will function as an intercollegiate ultimate frisbee team representing the University of Rochester, therefore promoting school spirit both on campus and at other schools. Also since ultimate frisbee requires running, jumping, disc throwing skills, timing, and coordination, it promotes athleticism. name: Wrestling and Judo
description: We provide an outlet for all students interested in wrestling and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu. We provide practice and competition for experienced individuals, as well as exercise and instruction for those who are inexperienced in a safe and supervised environment. Follow the Club on Instagram - @RocTheMats

name: Writing, Speaking, and Argument Program
description: The Writing, Speaking, and Argument Program helps students develop as academic communicators through courses, clusters, and minor tracks. It is home to the Writing and Speaking Center, which offers tutoring and support for undergraduate and graduate students.

name: WRUR 88.5
description: WRUR is a student-run radio & TV station designed to provide diverse multimedia content, experiential learning, and leadership to the student body and greater Rochester area.

name: Xclusive Step Team
description: Founded in 2006, Xclusive Step Team prides itself on being the only Non-Greek affiliated step team on campus. We believe that it is our responsibility to entertain crowds on & off campus, as well as teach people the culture from which stepping developed. In our performances, we value high energy, attitude, and precision. We build on the confidence, creativity, and personality of our members, encouraging them to be outspoken and unapologetically themselves. Be on the lookout for our workshops!

name: Yellowjacket Aero Design
description: Our Aero Design club promotes hands-on learning and collaboration in aerospace engineering, engaging members in all stages of airplane design, development, and testing. We focus on building skills in aerodynamics, CAD, and teamwork, while fostering innovation and professional growth through challenging projects.

name: YellowJackets
description: The University of Rochester YellowJackets is an auditioned traditionally all-male a cappella singing group founded in 1956 as a subset of the University of Rochester's original Men's Glee Club. The group provides its members with the opportunity to engage in music primarily through a cappella vocal performance. The YellowJackets aim to contribute to the enrichment of musical culture at the University of Rochester, the city of Rochester, nationally, and abroad whenever possible through a consistent commitment to the creation of excellent music.
